original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for familial British dementia located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for familial British dementia located?
final_qi.long_answer: Familial British dementia is caused by a stop-codon mutation in the ITM2B (BRI2) gene. This gene is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 13 (region 13q14), establishing chromosome 13 as the locus responsible for the disease.
